 O R D E R
1.The
petitioner herein is the accused in C.C.No.1198 of 2014 on the file of the Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, Koothuparamba.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, Koothuparamba
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the said proceeding, the petitioner faces prosecution for having committed offence punishable under Section 16 (1) (a) (i) read with Section 7 (i) and 2(ia)(m) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as "the PFA Act" for short) and under Rule 5 Appendix BA 17-01 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as "the PFA Rules" for short).
The aforesaid proceeding is sought to be quashed invoking the powers of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Yahia.N. (Nadukkandiyil) vs Food Inspector on 17 December, 2010 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26864500/
2 2.The prosecution allegation is that on 10.11.2010, the Food Inspector, Koothuparamba Circle,

entities.text: Yahia.N. (Nadukkandiyil) vs Food Inspector on 17 December, 2010 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: inspected
AS Oil & Flour Mill run by the petitioner and purchased 1500 ml of coconut oil for the purpose of analysis
. The said sample was sealed and labelled in accordance with the provisions of the Act and Rules.

One sample was forwarded to the Public Analyst, Regional Analytical Lab,
Calicut, for the purpose of analysis.
The report revealed that the sample did not conform to the standards prescribed for coconut oil falling under Item No. A.17.01 of Appendix B of the Rules and is therefore adulterated.

entities.text: Item No. A.17.01 of Appendix B
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: Consequent to the same, Annexure-A2 complaint was filed before the court below.
3.Heard learned counsel appearing for the petitioner as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.

4.The learned counsel submits that a Division Bench of this Court in Rasheed N.K. v. Food Inspector, Thalassery (2016 (1) KLD 704) after relying on the ratio of the judgment of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd v. Food Inspector and another [2010 (4) KLT 706 (SC)],
has laid down that Section 23 (1A) (ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act are mandatory, and any prosecution instituted under the Act, in violation of the said provisions cannot be sustained.

entities.text: Rasheed N.K. v. Food Inspector, Thalassery (2016 (1) KLD 704)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings Pvt. Ltd v. Food Inspector and another [2010 (4) KLT 706 (SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to the learned Counsel, the method of analysis adopted by the Public Analyst is not a validated one as prescribed under S.23 (1A) (hh) and the laboratory where the analysis was conducted was not a defined one for such examination under S.23 (1A) (ee) of the Act.
5.The learned Public Prosecutor would counter the submissions and would content that the principles laid down cannot be extended to the case on hand.
It is further submitted that these aspects are to be raised before the trial Court and sought for dismissal of the petition .
6.I have considered the rival submissions.
Admittedly, the complaint was laid solely on the strength of the Annexure- A1 report of the Public Analyst.
The said report is dated 17.12.2010.
It was found that the food item is adulterated as it did not conform to the standards prescribed for coconut oil falling under Item No. A.17.01 of Appendix B of the Rules.

The Division Bench in Rasheed N.K.
(Supra), after interpreting the various provisions of Act 37 of 1954, in line with the pronouncement of the Apex Court in Pepsico Case (Supra), has held that in order for the Analyst report to become the basis for launching a successful prosecution, the analysis of the food has to be conducted in a laboratory defined under S. 23 (1A) (ee) of the Act.
7.It is beyond dispute that Act 37 of 1954 was repealed as per the notification issued by the Central Government dated 04.08.2011 by virtue of powers under S. 97 (1) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
and the same had come into force on and from 05.08.2011.
It has been laid in Rasheed N.K. (Supra) that till repealing of Act 37 of 1954 no laboratory had been defined in terms of S.23 (1A) (ee) of the Act 37 of 1954.
In the case on hand the report is dated 17.12.2010 which in other words means that the laboratory where the analysis was conducted could not have been a defined lab.
If that be the case the taking of cognizance on the basis of the said report cannot be sustained.
The continuance of prosecution on the basis of Annexure-A21 complaint cannot be sustained as it is nothing but an abuse of process of law.
